what: Input pipeline latency of a DJI FPV Remote Controller 3, Gamepad API vs WebHID, on a local release drawing scan 39e63ce9 in this PC's Chrome at its 30 Hz display (the owner's item 7). Fake controller in the page: the roll stick changes at known moments E; per edge: delivery = first arrival in FlightSession.input - E, stamp = the page time the physics applies it at - E, frame = first animation frame at or after the arrival - E (ms). busy25: 25 ms of main-thread load per frame. Control hid-late20: 20 ms of added dispatch delay must show as ~20 ms more delivery.

findings: The gamepad is not polled once per display frame: at 30 Hz (33.3 ms frames) a change reaches the page in 0.9 ms median (p90 2.8) before and 1.5 ms (p90 4.7) after; WebHID 3.6 / 2.8 ms (its 160 Hz reports). The Gamepad API path is not slower than WebHID in the page.

Under 25 ms of main-thread load per frame both paths deliver late (gamepad p50 10.6 / p90 25.3, WebHID 13.7 / 25.3 ms) and, before the fix, the physics applied the gamepad move at the poll time: stamp error = delivery. After: the gamepad stamp error is 0 / 0 / 0 ms (p50 / p90 / max) in both runs; the WebHID stamp is the event time (Chrome stamps it when the page handles it), unchanged.

What the pilot sees is bound by the display: the first frame that can show a change comes 17-25 ms after it (median) on this 30 Hz display, the same on both paths; the display then adds its own scan-out.

Not measurable here: the DJI controller's own delay between a stick move and its USB report (its sampling, any filtering in simulator mode), and Chrome's gamepad thread delay; both need the real controller (and a camera or a photodiode).
